Neugebauer, the co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc., has issued a statement in response to the company's decision to drop its lawsuit against him, which was filed to validate a 70% supermajority bylaw amendment. The lawsuit's dismissal comes after a Texas Business Court ordered Fermi to produce documents and testimony explaining the rationale for the bylaw amendment, and Neugebauer claims that the company's actions confirm that the bylaw move was about entrenching the board's power rather than good governance. Neugebauer's claims challenging the validity of the bylaw remain alive and he will continue to pursue discovery and depositions of key players.

general.title: Modi’s Developed Nation Goal Remains on Track, Top Official Says
general.summary: India’s economy can approach $20 trillion by 2046 if it continues growing at its current pace, a top government official said, putting it in reach of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s goal of becoming a developed nation.

general.title: India’s ONGC Reviews Assets in Venezuela After US Green Light
general.summary: A team from the international investment arm of India’s Oil & Natural Gas Corp. has arrived in Venezuela to review assets in the country, according to people familiar with the matter, weeks after the company received a green light from the US.

general.title: BlackRock: $2.1T in GCC Capex By End of Decade
general.summary: BlackRock Investment Institute’s Ben Powell says the Middle East conflict is likely to accelerate the GCC’s push toward economic resilience, diversification and greater self-reliance. He told Horizons Middle East and Africa he expects more regional capital to be deployed domestically, with investment spanning infrastructure, AI, energy and security as Gulf states seek to reduce their exposure to strategic choke points while still generating attractive returns. (Source: Bloomb

general.title: Major: Treasury Market Is Functioning Normally
general.summary: Tradition Dubai Global Macro Advisor Steven Major says the global bond selloff is being driven largely by shifting interest-rate expectations rather than dysfunction or fiscal stress in the US Treasury market. He joined Horizons Middle East and Africa and discussed how persistently high oil prices could force further central-bank tightening, the risks to the dollar if the US economy cools, and why geopolitical anxiety has become a “new normal” for markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Renault-Backed Wandercraft Seeks €100 Million in New Funding
general.summary: Wandercraft, the French robotics startup backed by Renault SA, is seeking about €100 million ($116 million) in fresh funding to expand its business, people with knowledge of the matter said.

general.title: Bond Yields at 5% to 5.25% Pose Risk to Stocks: JPMorgan Private Bank
general.summary: Grace Peters, global investment strategy co-head at JPMorgan Private Bank, discusses risks facing investors, including rising bond yields, and why she sees markets ultimately climbing the "wall of worry." Peters speaks on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Energy Angst to Keep Pushing Yields Higher: 3-Minutes MLIV
general.summary: Anna Edwards, Lizzy Burden and Adam Linton break down today's key themes for analysts and investors on "Bloomberg: The Opening Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Germany on Track to Grow by as Much as 1%, Nagel Tells Le Monde
general.summary: Germany’s economy could expand by 1% this year, twice the pace projected only three months ago, Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel told Le Monde.

general.title: Shadow Lenders in India Line Up Over $1 Billion in Rupee Bonds
general.summary: India’s shadow lenders are set to raise at least 100 billion rupees ($1.1 billion) through the issuance of local-currency bonds as early as next week, according to people familiar with the matter, as they race to lock in borrowing costs before they rise further.

general.title: Russia Pauses Grain Export Duty as Black Sea Exports Stall
general.summary: Russia suspended the floating export duty on wheat, barley and corn through the end of 2026 as Ukrainian attacks disrupted shipments through the Black and Azov seas, affecting routes for more than 70% of exports.

general.summary: Nordea Bank Abp raised its economic forecasts for most of the Nordic region through next year due to better-than-expected resilience to higher energy prices, geopolitical tensions and global trade disruption.

general.title: Phison Electronics Sees Worst NAND Shortage in 2027
general.summary: Phison Electronics Corporation Co-Founder and CEO KS Pua believes NAND flash memory may face its worst shortage next year. He also discusses NAND's role in artificial intelligence. Phison Electronics designs, makes and sells controller chips for NAND flash memory used in solid-state drives , USB drives and memory cards. He speaks with Stephen Engle from the sidelines of 'Semicon Taiwan 2026'. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Biggest Thai Fund Sees More Gains for Banks, Data-Center Plays
general.summary: Thailand’s dividend-paying banks and developers riding the data-center boom are attractive options for investors seeking shelter from bouts of selling in other markets, according to the nation’s largest private money manager.

general.summary: Global data center spending is set to reach $31.6 trillion through 2050 to meet the world’s growing appetite for AI, an investment boom with no precedent in history, according to PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP.
